findings.title: Analytics has no consent-mode signalling and no documented event/retention governance
evidence: apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx:58-69 — GA is initialised with `gtag('config', '${GA_ID}')` (line 66) and no `gtag('consent', ...)` call or consent state; the script loads for every public page
grep for gtag('consent')/Consent Mode across apps/web (app, components, lib, middleware.ts) at 8d299b8d — zero hits; the only consent code in the app is the contact/intake form checkbox

apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:88-93 — the only retention statement defers analytics retention to Google Analytics' settings; no retention basis for the first-party store_analytics_events table
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:129-135 — the retention task purges only audit_logs and notifications; no store_analytics_events purge exists anywhere in apps/worker
apps/web/lib/catalog/data/analytics-events.json:37-43 — privacy rules exist in the storefront event registry, but no governance document (event catalog, purpose, retention) exists under docs/
git log 9c0b88c..8d299b8d -- apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx — empty; nothing changed since the prior run's verification
findings.impact: Analytics collection cannot be shown to be lawful or minimal: there is no consent-state contract, no per-event purpose/retention documentation, and no retention for the first-party analytics store.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a consent-state contract (gtag consent mode + a cookie/analytics opt-out), document each event's purpose and retention in a governance doc, and add a retention task for store_analytics_events.
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (verification duty, previous area AN row AN-P3-001): evidence unchanged from 9c0b88c; no commit in 9c0b88c..8d299b8d touches the layout, analytics route, or privacy page. The event registry partially exists but does not close the governance gap.

findings.title: Google Analytics and Tawk.to load on public pages with no cookie-consent or opt-out gate
evidence: apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx:58-69 — the GA script and gtag init render unconditionally whenever NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID is set
apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx:71-78 — the Tawk.to embed renders unconditionally whenever NEXT_PUBLIC_TAWKTO_ID is set
grep for CookieBanner/cookie-consent/consent components in apps/web at 8d299b8d — no cookie banner or consent component exists; the only consent UI is the contact/intake form checkbox
apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:54-81,96-110 — the policy names GA/Tawk.to but provides no cookie disclosure, no opt-out control, and no consent mechanism
apps/web/.env.example:9-10 — NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID / NEXT_PUBLIC_TAWKTO_ID are documented; docs/MARKETING_SITE_INTEGRATION.md:20-21 records live GA/Tawk.to IDs as in use

Production exercise is unverified: .github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:330-341 (web build args) and infra/digitalocean/docker-compose.yml:186-194 (web env) do not deliver NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID / NEXT_PUBLIC_TAWKTO_ID, so whether the scripts load on the deployed site depends on out-of-repo Vercel/operator config
findings.impact: Whenever the IDs are configured, GA and Tawk.to set cookies and process visitor data before any consent or opt-out, exposing the operator to GDPR/ePrivacy consent exposure. The ungated code path is the same one the privacy policy describes as active.
findings.recommendation: Gate third-party scripts on an explicit consent state (load after opt-in or use Google Consent Mode default-denied), add a cookie banner with accept/reject, and document the opt-out in the privacy policy.
findings.note: Re-verified at 8d299b8d (verification duty, previous area PRIV row PRIV-P2-001; subject matter is the analytics-script loading owned by this domain): both script blocks remain unconditional; no consent gate was added and no commit in 9c0b88c..8d299b8d touches layout.tsx. Cross-listed so the aggregator can dedupe against the privacy domain if it re-emits the same row.

findings.title: Analytics API stores visitor IP and user-agent in plaintext despite the documented no-PII contract
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:32-45 — POST /api/v1/analytics/track inserts `ip_address: req.ip ...` (line 43) and `user_agent: (req.headers['user-agent'] ...)` (line 44) for every event, unauthenticated
apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:22 — `metadata: z.record(z.unknown()).optional()` accepts an unbounded arbitrary JSON object; only the 10mb global body limit bounds it (apps/api/src/app.ts:110-120)
docs/modules/analytics.md:9,28 — the module doc states 'Public events are tracked anonymously (no PII)' and 'Tracking events contain no PII (page/category/product identifiers only)'

apps/web/lib/catalog/data/analytics-events.json:37-43 — the registry's own privacyRules say 'Hash or omit IP/user-agent if not needed' and 'Avoid capturing full intake free text in analytics metadata'
supabase/migrations/5302106_store_analytics.sql:13-14 — the table carries ip_address and user_agent columns; it has no organization_id
apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:67-71 — the admin list returns select('*') (including IP/UA) for the most recent 500 events
findings.impact: Visitor IP addresses and user agents are collected and retained by a public endpoint with no consent and no operational need (the registry explicitly says to omit/hash them). The implementation contradicts two committed contracts (module doc and event registry privacy rules), and the arbitrary metadata field allows sensitive payloads to be stored under an analytics event name.
findings.recommendation: Drop or hash ip_address/user_agent in the insert and the schema, replace metadata with a typed per-event schema (or cap keys/size), update docs/modules/analytics.md to match, and add a regression test asserting no raw PII is written.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Complements the domain-06 finding on admin read scoping: this is about collection/storage and the no-PII documentation contradiction.

findings.title: Storefront analytics capture is dead: the browser helper is never called and cannot pass the CSRF gate
evidence: apps/web/lib/catalog/analytics.ts:15-32 — track() POSTs to /api/v1/analytics/track without an X-CSRF-Token header (fetch at lines 24-28)
apps/api/src/middleware/csrf.ts:40-46,59-66,81-89 — /api/v1/analytics/track is not in the skip lists; a cookie-less or header-less POST is rejected 403 CSRF_INVALID
apps/api/src/app.ts:150 — csrfProtection is mounted globally before the routers (analytics router mounted at line 231)
grep for the helper across apps/web/app, components and lib at 8d299b8d — zero call sites of track(); only the unit test imports it
packages/sdk/src/client.ts:161-166 — the SDK sends X-CSRF-Token when the host supplies one, showing the intended pattern the web helper omits

docs/modules/analytics.md:13 documents 'POST /api/v1/analytics/track — anonymous event tracking from the storefront' as a live feature; apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/analytics/page.tsx:14-18 renders only the static registry, not the API data
apps/api/src/__tests__/analytics.test.ts:59-69 — the route test passes only because createTestApp (apps/api/src/__tests__/helpers.ts:83-93) does not mount csrfProtection
findings.impact: No storefront analytics events are captured: the helper has no callers and would 403 if called, the admin dashboard cards are never populated, and the documented product-analytics pipeline is unexercised. Any operator trusting the module doc or dashboard will overestimate the analytics coverage.
findings.recommendation: Wire track() into storefront views and send the CSRF token (or deliberately exempt this public path and document why), add an E2E that asserts a row lands in store_analytics_events, or remove the dead surface and correct the docs.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; static analysis only (no running stack was exercised).

findings.title: First-party analytics events have no retention or purge path
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:129-135 — the scheduled retention task purges only audit_logs and notifications
grep for store_analytics in apps/worker at 8d299b8d — zero hits; no task purges store_analytics_events
supabase/migrations/5302106_store_analytics.sql:1-25 — the table has no retention policy or TTL
apps/worker/src/tasks/public-interaction-retention.ts:5-24 and apps/worker/src/main.ts:71-76 — public_interactions already has a daily 90-day purge, the pattern store analytics lacks

apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:88-93 — the policy promises retention only for contact submissions (3 years) and defers analytics retention to Google Analytics; the first-party analytics store is not covered
findings.impact: IP address, user-agent and arbitrary metadata rows would be retained indefinitely (storage-limitation/GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) exposure), and the table grows without bound. If capture is later wired (finding above), this becomes a live privacy issue.
findings.recommendation: Add a store_analytics_events retention task (e.g. 90-400 days, mirroring public-interaction-retention) or drop the PII columns, and document per-store retention in the privacy policy and the analytics module doc.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; this is the analytics-specific instance of the generic DATA-P2-006 'several stores lack a retention policy' row owned by the data domain.

findings.title: Anonymous direct inserts to store_analytics_events bypass API validation, rate limits, and retention
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302106_store_analytics.sql:24-25 — CREATE POLICY anon_insert FOR INSERT TO anon WITH CHECK (true)
supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:73 — grant insert on table public.store_analytics_events to anon
apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:13-24 — input validation (event name, field lengths, metadata shape) only applies on the API path
apps/api/src/app.ts:125-146 — the 300/15min per-IP limiter applies to the API, not to direct Supabase anon writes
apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:64-78 — admin list cannot distinguish API-written rows from direct inserts
findings.impact: Anyone holding the public anon key can write arbitrary analytics rows (event, ip_address, user_agent, metadata) directly to the table, poisoning product analytics and growing an unretained table outside every API control. The API route already exists, so the direct-write grant is redundant attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Revoke the anon INSERT grant/policy (keep writes on the API path) or add DB-level constraints (event allow-list, column limits); keep the least-privilege migration as the single source of truth.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; static analysis. Anon-key exposure in the deployed web app was not verified (the web app calls the API, not Supabase directly).

findings.title: Visitor-alert tracking collects IP/geo before consent and sends the visitor IP to ip-api.com over plaintext HTTP
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:47-87 — GET /public/init is unauthenticated and stores ip_address, location, user_agent, platform and referrer in public_interactions
apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:64 — the geolocation lookup uses `http://ip-api.com/json/${cleanIp}` (plaintext HTTP) and the visitor IP is interpolated into the URL
apps/web/components/marketing/ContactForm.tsx:43-51 — /public/init fires on component mount, before any user action; the consent checkbox (lines 313-327) gates only the submit button (line 333)
apps/web/components/store/IntakeFormRenderer.tsx:46 — the store intake form does the same pre-consent init call
apps/web/app/(public)/contact/actions.ts:21-25 — consent is checked only for the lead submission and is dropped before the API call
apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:105,177,221-226 — visitor location/platform/referrer go to a Teams webhook and IP/UA/location/referrer go into a JSM ticket after submit

apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:77-80 — the policy discloses ip-api.com but asserts 'No data is permanently stored by ip-api.com' (unverifiable) and does not describe the pre-submission tracking
findings.impact: Every contact-page visitor's IP address is disclosed to a third-party geo service in cleartext and stored/forwarded by MCT before any consent is given; the consent checkbox does not cover the tracking that already happened. The cleartext third-party transfer is a privacy and interception exposure.
findings.recommendation: Use HTTPS for the geo lookup (or remove the third-party lookup), defer /public/init until consent is captured (or make the tracking explicitly consent-independent and document it), record consent server-side, and add a test that no pre-consent third-party call occurs.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; the 90-day public_interactions retention (public-interaction-retention.ts) and bot filter (bot-detection.ts) are acknowledged mitigations, but they do not address consent or the cleartext transfer.

findings.title: Consent is not recorded and the privacy policy omits first-party tracking stores and opt-out mechanics
evidence: apps/web/app/(public)/contact/actions.ts:25 — `const { consent: _, ...payload } = data;` discards the consent flag; it is never persisted
apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:13-24 — the submit schema has no consent field, so the API cannot record when/which policy version was accepted

apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:54-81,96-110 — the policy lists GA/Tawk.to/Teams/JSM/ip-api.com and GDPR/CCPA rights, but has no cookie/analytics section, no opt-out control, and never mentions public_interactions or store_analytics_events
apps/web/components/store/IntakeFormRenderer.tsx:244-264 — the intake consent checkbox is client-side only and is not persisted either
findings.impact: There is no accountability record of consent (GDPR Art. 7) and no mechanism for a visitor to opt out of first-party analytics, while the policy under-describes the first-party tracking stores.
findings.recommendation: Persist consent (flag, timestamp, policy version) on the interaction/lead record, add a cookie/analytics opt-out to the public site, and document the first-party tracking stores and their retention in the privacy policy.

findings.title: Error telemetry has no explicit PII scrubbing, retention, or vendor disclosure
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/sentry.ts:8-13 — Sentry.init with dsn/environment/release/tracesSampleRate only; no sendDefaultPii, beforeSend, or scrub callback
apps/web/instrumentation-client.ts:12-17 and apps/web/sentry.server.config.ts:12-17 — same minimal init for the web app; no replay integration (session replay is absent — positive)
apps/api/src/lib/logger.ts:5-39 — the pino logger redacts email/phone/token/cookie fields, but that redaction does not apply to Sentry event payloads
apps/web/app/(public)/privacy/page.tsx:54-81 — Sentry is not listed in the third-party vendor list, and no retention or data-residency statement exists for error telemetry
findings.impact: Error events can carry request/user context to a third-party processor with no explicit scrubbing guarantee, no retention statement, and no policy disclosure; the operator cannot demonstrate data minimisation for telemetry.
findings.recommendation: Set sendDefaultPii:false explicitly, add a beforeSend scrubber for PII fields, document Sentry (and any other error processor) in the vendor list with retention, and add a test that error payloads drop email/phone/IP.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; the JS SDK defaults to sendDefaultPii:false, so exposure is not proven — this is a hardening/disclosure gap rather than a demonstrated leak. Session replay is absent, which is a strength.

Headline-claim checks (shared-rules sampling duty):

- "POST /analytics/track — anonymous event tracking from the storefront" is a working feature (`docs/modules/analytics.md:13`) — **partially supported**: endpoint + tests exist, but no caller and the browser helper cannot pass CSRF → not reproducible end-to-end.
- "GA + Tawk.to fire on every marketing page visit" (`docs/MARKETING_SITE_INTEGRATION.md:269`) — **code path supported, production exercise unverified** (IDs are not delivered by the deploy pipeline).
- "The 90-day retention task bounds table growth" for `public_interactions` (`docs/VISITOR_ALERTS.md`) — **supported** (`public-interaction-retention.ts:5-24`, scheduled in `main.ts:71-76`); note there is no equivalent for `store_analytics_events`.

## Executive Summary

Strengths: the public marketing layout is the only place third-party analytics load (admin/portal layouts load none); the scripts are env-gated, CSP-nonce'd, and Tawk.to is `crossOrigin="anonymous"`; there is no session replay, no tracking pixel, and no analytics SDK beyond GA4 + Tawk.to; the event registry documents 20 events and privacy rules; `public_interactions` has a 90-day purge and bot filtering; the contact and intake forms gate submission on a consent checkbox; the API logger redacts PII fields.

Risks: (1) GA4 and Tawk.to load with no consent or opt-out, and there is no consent-mode signalling; (2) the public analytics endpoint stores visitor IP/user-agent and arbitrary metadata in plaintext, contradicting the module doc and the registry's own privacy rules; (3) storefront event capture is dead — no call sites and a CSRF gate the helper cannot pass; (4) first-party analytics rows have no retention; (5) contact-page visitor tracking sends the visitor IP to ip-api.com over plaintext HTTP before consent; (6) consent is never recorded and the privacy policy omits first-party tracking stores and opt-out.

Recommended next actions (ordered): fix the no-PII contract or the code; add consent mode + a cookie/opt-out; wire or remove storefront capture; add analytics retention; move the geo lookup to HTTPS and behind consent; persist consent and extend the policy.

## Detailed Review

### Item: GA4 embed and consent mode

- Evidence: `apps/web/app/(public)/layout.tsx:58-69`; `apps/web/middleware.ts:58-96` (nonce).
- What it does: loads `gtag.js` after interactive and runs `gtag('config', ID)` for every public page when `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_ID` is set.
- Missing controls: no `gtag('consent', 'default', ...)`, no opt-out, no banner.
- Risks: consent exposure in the EU/EEA/UK and California opt-out expectations; the privacy policy describes GA as active.
- Recommended improvement: consent-mode default-denied + banner; document opt-out.
- Suggested tests: unit test asserting the consent script precedes config when a consent flag is false; E2E asserting no GA request before accept.
- Suggested docs: privacy policy cookie section; `docs/modules/analytics.md`.

### Item: Tawk.to embed

- Evidence: `layout.tsx:71-78`.
- Same class as GA: loads on every public page whenever the ID is configured, with no consent gate.

### Item: Public track endpoint and payload

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:13-61`; `docs/modules/analytics.md:9,28`; `analytics-events.json:37-43`.
- What it does: validates `event` plus optional ids/metadata and inserts a row with `ip_address` and `user_agent` from the request.
- Missing controls: consent, PII minimisation, typed metadata, tenant/purpose model.
- Risks: PII retention without basis; documentation contradicts code.

### Item: Storefront capture wiring (CSRF)

- Evidence: `apps/web/lib/catalog/analytics.ts:15-32`; `apps/api/src/middleware/csrf.ts:81-89`; `apps/api/src/app.ts:150`.
- What it does: helper posts without CSRF header; no component calls it.
- Risks: product analytics is not captured; docs and dashboard cards overstate coverage.

### Item: Visitor alerts (`/public/init`)

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:47-125`; `ContactForm.tsx:43-51`; `docs/VISITOR_ALERTS.md`.
- What it does: stores IP/UA/platform/referrer, looks up geo via `http://ip-api.com`, optionally alerts Teams.
- Missing controls: consent, HTTPS for the third-party lookup.
- Mitigations already present: bot filter, 30-min alert dedupe, 90-day retention.

### Item: Consent recording

- Evidence: `apps/web/app/(public)/contact/actions.ts:21-25`; `apps/api/src/routes/public.ts:13-24`.
- What it does: blocks submit without the checkbox, then drops the flag; API has no consent field.

### Item: Retention

- Evidence: `apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:129-135`; `public-interaction-retention.ts:5-24`.
- What it does: purges audit_logs + notifications daily and public_interactions at 90 days; store analytics has no purge.

### Item: Error telemetry

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/lib/sentry.ts:8-13`; web sentry configs; `apps/api/src/lib/logger.ts:5-39`.
- What it does: sends errors/traces to Sentry when a DSN is set; no explicit PII scrubbing in the Sentry path; logger redaction is separate.

## Findings

IDs are assigned by the aggregator; titles below match the JSON.

1. **Analytics has no consent-mode signalling and no documented event/retention governance** (P3, still-open — verification of prior `AN-P3-001`). Re-verified at `8d299b8d`: unchanged.
2. **Google Analytics and Tawk.to load on public pages with no cookie-consent or opt-out gate** (P2, still-open — verification of prior `PRIV-P2-001`, cross-listed from area PRIV). Re-verified at `8d299b8d`: unchanged.
3. **Analytics API stores visitor IP and user-agent in plaintext despite the documented no-PII contract** (P2, open). New.
4. **Storefront analytics capture is dead: the browser helper is never called and cannot pass the CSRF gate** (P2, open). New.
5. **First-party analytics events have no retention or purge path** (P2, open). New.
6. **Anonymous direct inserts to store_analytics_events bypass API validation, rate limits, and retention** (P3, open). New.
7. **Visitor-alert tracking collects IP/geo before consent and sends the visitor IP to ip-api.com over plaintext HTTP** (P2, open). New.
8. **Consent is not recorded and the privacy policy omits first-party tracking stores and opt-out mechanics** (P3, open). New.
9. **Error telemetry has no explicit PII scrubbing, retention, or vendor disclosure** (P3, open). New.

Cross-references (not duplicated): the undefined `get_analytics_summary` RPC and the tenant-scoping of admin analytics reads were re-verified by domain 06 (`06_security_authz_tenancy_audit.json`); the platform-wide store/analytics admin surface by domain 25; search-query analytics by domain 31; generic retention ownership by domain 07.
